selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: Why did the traveler want to enter the human world at this point in his journey?
questions.answer: He wanted to move higher in knowing Allah through more stages of faith and understanding.

questions.question: How does the passage show that the prophets were united?
questions.answer: It shows them all giving the same call to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: How were the prophets helping people rise above a lower way of living?
questions.answer: They taught belief in Allah so people could become spiritually better and nobler.

questions.question: According to the passage, what was one goal of the prophets in teaching people?
questions.answer: They aimed to raise people from a low, animal-like condition to a high, angel-like level.

questions.question: What role did large numbers of believers play in confirming the prophets?
questions.answer: Their acceptance showed that the prophets’ message convinced many honest people.

questions.question: What moral judgment does the passage make about denying that truth?
questions.answer: It judges denial of it as a grave wrongdoing.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the mistake of those who reject a truth confirmed by so many truthful witnesses?
questions.answer: It describes their rejection as a very serious wrong and even a crime.

questions.question: How do the results seen in the prophets’ students support the prophets’ teachings?
questions.answer: Their students reached truth and spiritual excellence, showing the teachings were effective and true.

questions.question: Why is the agreement of all prophets and their followers especially important?
questions.answer: Because united agreement among so many sincere people makes the proof very strong.

questions.question: What did the traveler gain from the prophets’ lessons?
questions.answer: He gained a strong benefit to his faith.

questions.question: What was the traveler trying to increase as he moved forward in his journey?
questions.answer: He was trying to increase his knowledge of Allah.

questions.question: Which human group is given the highest place in this part of the passage?
questions.answer: The prophets are given the highest place.

questions.question: What common act were all the prophets doing when the traveler saw them?
questions.answer: They were all remembering Allah and calling people to His oneness.

questions.question: What does the image of the traveler kneeling in a school suggest about his attitude?
questions.answer: It suggests humility, respect, and readiness to learn.

questions.question: Besides miracles, what public evidence supported the prophets?
questions.answer: Many people believed them and confirmed their message.

questions.question: Why does the passage emphasize that these followers were truthful and serious?
questions.answer: Because trustworthy people agreeing on something makes that claim more reliable.

questions.question: What does the passage say such rejection deserves?
questions.answer: It says such a serious wrong deserves a serious punishment.

questions.question: How do the prophets’ good character and excellent qualities function in the argument?
questions.answer: They serve as signs that the prophets were sincere and trustworthy.

questions.question: What does the agreement among prophets and their followers show?
questions.answer: It shows harmony in the message and mutual support in the truth.

questions.question: Why is belief in all prophets called a source of strength?
questions.answer: Because accepting all of them makes faith more complete and firmly grounded.

questions.question: What new realm did the traveler wish to enter after advancing in knowledge of Allah?
questions.answer: He wished to enter the world of human beings.

questions.question: When he looked toward earlier times, whom did he see first among people?
questions.answer: He saw the prophets first.

questions.question: What kind of education were the prophets giving to people?
questions.answer: They were giving spiritual and moral guidance that led people to belief in Allah.

questions.question: How does the acceptance of the prophets by whole communities help the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that many people were convinced by clear signs and truthful teaching.
